headline: Attackers exploited a Metabase SQL injection zero-day to breach Framework and Tally as a vishing and social-engineering wave struck Wall Street firms, Levi Strauss, and North Carolina's ports.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep beating technology by working the humans, as UNC6671 callers impersonate IT help desks to employees' personal phones and social engineers talk three Levi Strauss workers into surrendering corporate data.
emerging_trends.topic_title: UNC6671 Vishing Extortion Rebrands as BlackFile Splinters

emerging_trends.text: Decades-old code keeps yielding fresh compromises, from an 18-year-old Linux SCTP flaw that grants root to a Metabase SQL injection that attackers exploited to breach Framework and Tally.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Metabase SQL Injection Zero-Day Breaches Framework and Tally

emerging_trends.text: Criminals now let AI generate the camouflage, flooding npm with nearly 800 AI-named typosquatted packages that drop a cross-platform remote access trojan and infostealer.

topics.title: New Critical Bugs Span WordPress, Linux, and LoadMaster
topics.latest_developments: WordPress patched a pre-authentication reflected XSS, CVE-2026-64638 at CVSS 8.9, that pwn.ai chained into PHP code execution and that affects every version; Tencent researchers turned an 18-year-old Linux SCTP use-after-free into root and a container escape, fixed in kernels 7.1.6, 6.18.42, 6.12.101, and 6.6.148; CISA added Progress LoadMaster command injection CVE-2026-8037 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog; and Microsoft, Apple, and Chrome 151 shipped fresh fixes.
topics.summary: A dense batch of high-severity flaws hit web, operating-system, and load-balancer software, one already under active exploitation. Administrators should prioritize the LoadMaster and WordPress fixes and update older Linux kernels running SCTP.

sources.title: New WordPress Pre-Auth XSS Could Lead to PHP Code Execution - Patch ASAP
18-Year-Old Linux SCTP Flaw Could Let Local Users Gain Root and Escape Containers
CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog
Microsoft, Apple Release Fresh Security Updates

topics.title: UNC6671 Vishing Extortion Rebrands as BlackFile Splinters
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek and The Hacker News reported that UNC6671, which first called itself BlackFile, has expanded into the Redact, Pink, Helix, and Falcon brands and now calls employees on their personal phones, posing as IT help desk staff running urgent security migrations to steal SaaS data.
topics.summary: UNC6671 is a data-extortion crew hitting financial services, private equity, and professional services firms through voice phishing. Verify any help-desk request for credentials or migration steps through a separate, trusted channel.

sources.title: Vishing Extortion Group UNC6671 Rebrands After Making Millions
UNC6671 Vishing Attacks Target Personal Phones to Steal SaaS Data

topics.title: Levi Strauss and North Carolina Ports Confirm Attacks
topics.latest_developments: Levi Strauss & Co. said hackers socially engineered three employees to reach and steal corporate data from their machines, and the North Carolina State Ports Authority confirmed a cyberattack that disrupted IT systems and slowed operations at the Port of Wilmington, the Port of Morehead City, and the Charlotte Inland Port.
topics.summary: Two unrelated incidents show attackers pairing employee manipulation with operational disruption. Levi Strauss lost corporate files to social engineering; North Carolina's ports saw cargo handling slow while responders worked to restore systems.

sources.title: Levi Strauss & Co. says hackers stole corporate data in cyberattack
North Carolina Ports confirms cyberattack disrupting operations

topics.title: Malicious npm Flood and TeamPCP's Long History
topics.latest_developments: OpenSourceMalware researcher Paul flagged nearly 800 npm packages using AI-generated typosquatted names that all deliver a cross-platform remote access trojan and infostealer to Windows, macOS, and Linux, while a separate analysis tied the TeamPCP actor's supply-chain campaign back to Redis server attacks running since 2020.
topics.summary: Attackers keep abusing npm's open publishing to seed convincing package names at scale, and TeamPCP shows how long a group can compromise internet-facing infrastructure before pivoting to the supply chain. Pin and audit dependencies rather than trusting names.

sources.title: Nearly 800 Malicious npm Packages Deliver Cross-Platform RAT and Infostealer
TeamPCP Linked To Redis Attacks Dating Back To 2020 And Later Supply Chain Campaign

topics.title: Senate Confirms Cyber Ambassador as EU AI Act Nears Enforcement
topics.latest_developments: The Senate confirmed NTIA official Adam Cassady as the State Department's ambassador-at-large for cyber policy, the second person to hold the post, while Veeam Field CTO Edwin Weijdema said the EU AI Act's Article 50 transparency rules will likely produce corrective orders more often than large fines in their first year.
topics.summary: Washington filled its top cyber-diplomacy role as Europe prepares to enforce AI transparency obligations, including rules on when an AI agent counts as interacting with a person. Enterprises should map where their AI systems disclose themselves to users.

sources.title: US cyber ambassador nominee Cassady confirmed in Senate
What the first year of EU AI Act transparency enforcement could look like

topics.title: Metabase SQL Injection Zero-Day Breaches Framework and Tally
topics.latest_developments: BleepingComputer reported that attackers exploited a critical Metabase SQL injection zero-day to hit self-hosted instances and steal data, naming laptop maker Framework and accounting app Tally among the victims.
topics.summary: Metabase is a widely deployed open-source business-intelligence tool; the flaw let attackers pull data directly from customer instances. Organizations running Metabase should patch immediately and hunt for signs of compromise.

sources.title: Metabase SQLi zero-day exploited in customer data-theft attacks
